description: Solo team from Purwokerto, Indonesia. We build EmberSight MR, a mixed-reality wildfire command table: a live globe of NASA FIRMS fires, a harmonized MODIS + VIIRS burning calendar, and 3D NASA terrain where fire spread, smoke and firefighter deployment are simulated.
summary: EmberSight MR turns two decades of NASA fire satellite records into a mixed-reality command table for wildfire responders. It answers the "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge with a web app that identifies, predicts and helps respond to fires. Identify: a 3D globe shows live NASA FIRMS VIIRS fires worldwide, and zooming into a region reveals a burning activity calendar (2000-2025) in which MODIS and VIIRS hotspots are harmonized onto one scale (VIIRS = 4.83 x MODIS, R2 = 0.98), so seasons can be compared regardless of sensor. Predict: tapping any fire builds a 3D surface from NASA SRTM terrain, Landsat imagery and NASA POWER hourly weather, then simulates how the fire spreads and which villages lie in the smoke path. Respond: the app recommends the smallest number of firefighting crews, where to place them and in what order, and plays the result back hour by hour against the no-action case. The same page runs in augmented reality on a phone or Meta Quest. We start with Kalimantan, Indonesia, where peat fires burn for months. Slides (7): https://embersight-mr.vercel.app/EmberSight_MR_slides.pptx
details:
WHAT IT DOES
EmberSight MR is a web app (desktop, phone and Meta Quest via WebXR) that follows one continuous zoom from the whole Earth down to a single fire.
1. Identify - Global: a 3D globe (NASA Blue Marble) shows every VIIRS (NOAA-20) active-fire detection of the last 7 days from NASA FIRMS, refreshed every 3 hours through a small serverless relay.
2. Identify - Regional: zooming toward Borneo fades in a sharper NASA MODIS scene and a burning activity calendar of monthly hotspots from 2000 to 2025 on one consistent, VIIRS-equivalent scale.
3. Predict - Surface: tapping any fire builds a 3D terrain of about 55 x 55 km around the nearest fire cluster in about 30 seconds, from NASA SRTM elevation, Landsat imagery and NDVI (NASA GIBS) and the latest 72 h of NASA POWER hourly wind, humidity, temperature and rain. A fire-spread simulation shows how the fire grows with no action, and a downwind cone lists the settlements in the smoke path.
4. Respond: users drop patrol units (5 people), squads (15) or task forces (30), or press Recommend. The app finds the smallest number of units that puts the fire out within the chosen time, where to place them and the order to send them, then plays both scenarios back hour by hour with the crews walking to the fire. Every run is kept in a comparison table.
5. Mixed reality: on a phone (ARCore) or Meta Quest the same page opens in AR on a real table: drag to rotate, pinch to zoom, tap the terrain to add a squad.

HOW IT WORKS
Harmonization: we filtered FIRMS MODIS C6.1 (confidence 30+, vegetation fires) and VIIRS S-NPP (nominal/high) hotspots to Indonesian Borneo and counted them per month. Over the 2012-2025 overlap, VIIRS counts are almost proportional to MODIS: VIIRS = 4.83 x MODIS (least squares, R2 = 0.98). The calendar uses VIIRS from 2012 and scaled MODIS before 2012, so 26 years compare directly. The worst seasons (2002, 2006, 2015 with about 350,000 hotspots, and 2019) all peak in August-October of dry El Nino years.
Fire spread: a cellular automaton on a 160 x 160 grid with 30-minute steps. Spread rises with fuel (Landsat NDVI), downwind alignment, uphill slope (SRTM) and dryness from NASA POWER humidity; rain damps it. Cells flame for 2-6 h and then smoulder (peat 36 h), so fires survive humid nights and revive the next afternoon. Crews arrive in priority order, protect their zone, put out burning cells, help neighbouring units and walk to the nearest remaining fire.
Example: South Kalimantan peat fire, 27 Sep 2023, 48 h: about 50 squads put the fire out, burning about 5.5k ha instead of 29.7k ha (about -81%), while the same number spread evenly fails to put it out.

WHO IT IS FOR
Fire brigades such as Indonesia's Manggala Agni, regional disaster agencies (BPBD) and community fire groups: prevention (when and where to stand by), response (where to send limited crews, whom to warn about smoke) and training on real past fire days.

TOOLS
JavaScript, three.js (WebGL/WebXR), Python (pandas, NumPy, Pillow), NASA GIBS WMS, NASA POWER API, NASA FIRMS, Vercel (static site plus one serverless function).

LIMITATIONS
The simulation is a simplified planning and training model, not an operational forecast; crew rates are model assumptions, not field-calibrated. Wind is about 50 km resolution and lags real time by a few days; Landsat WELD layers are older annual composites; SRTM covers 56S-60N.

NEXT STEPS
Forecast wind (GEOS-FP), a validated peat-fire model, smoke checks against aerosol data, village roads and water sources for logistics, and shared multi-user MR sessions.
